summary: Nonlinear system with 2 equilibrium points. Tap the phase plane to draw trajectories.

methods.name: Linearization at equilibria
methods.reason: The system is not of the form \(\mathbf{X}' = A\mathbf{X}\), so its behaviour is read off near each equilibrium point from the Jacobian.

steps.title: Find the equilibrium points
steps.text: Equilibria are where both right-hand sides are zero.

steps.title: Compute the Jacobian
steps.text: Near an equilibrium the system behaves like the linear system whose matrix is the Jacobian evaluated there.
latex: J = \begin{pmatrix} f_x & f_y\\ g_x & g_y \end{pmatrix} = \begin{pmatrix}1 - y & - x\\y & x - 1\end{pmatrix}

steps.title: Classify the equilibrium at (0, 0)
steps.text: The linearization is a saddle point: unstable.

steps.title: Classify the equilibrium at (1, 1)
steps.text: The linearization is a center: stable but not asymptotically stable. The linear terms alone do not settle the behaviour of the nonlinear system here.
